scope: Corrected post-pilot experiment designs for all 23 original provisional records. These follow-up stages have not been executed.
canonical_id_assignment: Only the existing campaign harness may assign immutable IDs; no hypothesis IDs were created here.
seed_policy: Use the harness for campaign-wide reservation; local pilot derivations are reproducible but not campaign-reserved.

common_protocol.instance_scope: Synthetic or known-answer small prime fields. No deployed keys or private-key recovery.
common_protocol.no_sieving: SNFS-B4 prohibits sieving under all circumstances.
common_protocol.evidence: Original theorem-closed records remain receipt-only. Measurements do not certify asymptotic lower bounds, universal impossibility, or subexponential ECDLP.
common_protocol.cost_accounting: Record input-generation costs separately; charge all algorithm-required setup, preprocessing, failed targets, output materialization, coordinate recovery, and verification. Report single-target and amortized costs separately.
common_protocol.statistics: Predeclare sample law, excluded exceptional strata and hypotheses. Use independent instances, held-out curves/sizes, confidence intervals, multiple-testing control where applicable, and explicit timeout censoring.
common_protocol.resources: Per-stage CPU caps below are proposed initial screening caps, not measured campaign costs or execution already completed.
common_protocol.dependencies: Sage/Magma or equivalent certified packages are still needed for full p-adic precision, number-field descent, general section solvers, Jacobian arithmetic and random-surface rank certification.

records.hypothesis: Universal polynomial identities persist under reduction; exceptional vanishing coefficients and implementation costs are measured separately.
steps: Build universal S3 and S4 over Z[a,b], then specialize 20 nonsingular curves per actual prime.
Pair pseudo-Mersenne and random primes at 13,17,23,31 bits; record vanished coefficients, degrees and factorization separately.
Only after A3's workload is fixed, time the complete matched decomposition operation and profile modular reduction.
controls: Identical curve coefficients where both reductions are nonsingular; paired root-generation policy and solver builds.
measurements: Support differences with exceptional coefficients identified
Full-operation timing ratio with confidence intervals
records.stopping_rule: Four sizes, 20 curves each; stop any solver run at 10 minutes. A timing ratio never becomes a theorem receipt.

records.hypothesis: A specified multivariate modular-lattice construction recovers planted S3 roots in a measurable bounded range; no generic Coppersmith theorem is assumed.
steps: First reproduce an independently specified bivariate linear bounded-root control, including its exact solution set, using the same scaling and recovery path.
Sweep S3 at 12,16,20,24 bits and beta=0.15..0.50 with at least 30 plants per cell; predeclare lattice shifts and vector-selection rules.
Increase lattice dimensions only after control success; add BKZ and S4 as separate gated stages.
controls: Exact enumerated roots at the smallest sizes
Independent bivariate linear control, not the univariate surrogate
Hold back planted coordinates from candidate selection and root recovery
measurements: Certified short-vector count and algebraic independence
Full wall time including lattice construction and recovery
records.stopping_rule: Do not interpret a beta threshold until the bivariate control passes. Cap each attempt at 60 seconds and this stage at 8 CPU-hours.

records.hypothesis: Compact compositional factor bases can improve completed decomposition costs relative to matched interval bases, without presuming that this improves a full DLP algorithm.
steps: Reproduce interval and repeated-power subgroup bases at five increasing small prime sizes, matched by actual factor-base cardinality.
Run m=2 then m=3 using enumeration, SAT and one algebraic solver with at least 30 planted and 30 fresh targets per cell.
Account for relation yield, factor-base construction, failed targets, and matrix costs before choosing a full index-calculus parameter set.
For a conventional full sparse matrix model, explore beta below 1/4 and larger m only if measured decomposition costs justify it.
controls: Actual elliptic decompositions verified after Semaev solving
Fresh targets separated from planted targets
Equal timeout, memory, solver build and arithmetic encoding
measurements: Projected relation and matrix costs with all assumptions explicit
records.stopping_rule: Initial cap 16 CPU-hours; stop a solver line after two consecutive cells with mostly censored attempts. No exponent claim from the current tiny SAT pilot.

records.hypothesis: Valid digit-ring factor bases show no practically useful closure beyond matched finite-subset effects.
steps: Use only d dividing n, with certified primes 2^n-c; select n from 12,18,20,24,30 and compatible d=2,3,5.
Measure closure on 20 curves per cell and compare with an ensemble of equal-size random subsets of E(Fp).
Specify a carry-aware digit encoding before measuring lifted S3 degree or factorization.
controls: Normalize by #E(Fp), include the identity convention, and account for P+(-P).
Matched random-prime and random-subset controls
measurements: Closure excess over the random-subset distribution
Actual digit polynomial size, degree and factorization
records.stopping_rule: Choose sample counts to make reference closure counts at least 1000; cap stage at 4 CPU-hours. A finite deviation alone is not a structural gain.

records.hypothesis: For a fixed good curve lift with p not dividing N, the torsion section is lift-independent; the unrescaled statistic is zero modulo p.
steps: Extend the checked p^2 implementation to precisions 5,10,20 using a validated p-adic package.
Distinguish changes of point lift on one fixed curve lift from changes of the curve model.
Add ramified-extension controls only with validated precision tracking.
controls: Exhaustive point-lift offsets at small p
Anomalous curves with explicitly identified curve lifts
Independent p-adic arithmetic implementation
measurements: Rescaled-statistic distribution under a stated sampling law
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; 1000 checks per cell, 4 CPU-hour cap. Do not replace the identically zero statistic by an unspecified information test.

records.hypothesis: Random anomalous-curve lifts usually give a nonzero Smart map; the correctly certified canonical deformation gives a zero map.
steps: Extend the four class-number-one cases to 20 small anomalous curves, including class number greater than one.
Certify the endomorphism order, local H_D root, reduction isomorphism and twist.
Check random and canonical lifts at multiple p-adic precisions.
controls: Known-answer logs
Non-anomalous curves
Random degenerate lifts tracked separately from certified canonical lifts
measurements: Success and degeneracy fractions with binomial intervals
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; 1000 random lifts per curve, 8 CPU-hour cap. A zero map at p^2 is not a full canonical-model certificate at all precisions.

records.hypothesis: A correctly defined generalized-Jacobian connecting map agrees with the Tate pairing in its quotient/reduced target.
steps: Implement divisor/function representatives and the connecting map independently of Miller arithmetic.
Specify the target Fq*/(Fq*)^ell, extension class and reduction convention.
Test k=1,2,3 with admissible nonzero classes and bad-class negative controls.
controls: Existing Miller bilinearity and nontriviality pilot
Extension classes divisible by ell should not be assumed nondegenerate
Support poles excluded by an explicit divisor convention
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; three primes per k, 1000 valid pairs each, 8 CPU-hour cap. Current evidence covers Miller controls only.

records.hypothesis: Special multiplicative polynomial selection can improve multiplicative-side norms, while useful pairing transfer still requires a suitable embedding degree.
steps: Extend embedding-order samples with normalized k/(ell-1), actual factorization costs and anomalous-case stratification.
If CADO tools are supplied, run standalone polyselect executables only, with equal optimization budgets and fixed Murphy-E conventions.
Keep public-parameter order certificates separate from synthetic DLP experiments.
controls: Matched subgroup-size strata
Known small-embedding-degree synthetic curves
Identical norm region and optimization budget
measurements: Murphy-E and norm metrics; L constants include cube roots
records.stopping_rule: No sieving under any circumstances. Never invoke a default complete CADO pipeline. Cap the initial extension at 8 CPU-hours; the original 24-hour polyselect comparison is a separate unrun stage.

records.hypothesis: The specified generalized-Jacobian kernels permit transfers only on their explicitly available primary components.
steps: Replace an unspecified full-modulus enumeration by degree/residue/multiplicity types whose completeness is proved.
Compute concrete extension classes and compare their ell-primary behavior with the finite cyclic-kernel quotient controls.
State the scope of Chevalley/Poincare arguments without converting them into general algorithmic lower bounds.
controls: B2 unipotent and B3 toric positive controls
Kernel types with ell not dividing their finite-point order
measurements: Transfer table with residue degrees and extension classes
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; three small primes, degree at most four, 4 CPU-hour cap. Abstract kernel quotients alone do not complete the generalized-Jacobian experiment.

records.hypothesis: Bounded-degree positive-dimensional cover-image constraints and compact zero-dimensional compositional factor bases have different size/cost behavior.
steps: Split the original claim into bounded-degree cover-image counts and zero-dimensional bases.
For cover families, certify absolute irreducibility, map degree and genus before applying point-count bounds.
For compositional bases, record circuit description size, cardinality and actual A3 decomposition cost.
controls: Repeated-squaring bases already measured
Extension-field subfield analogue
measurements: Point-image cardinality versus certified map degree
Decomposition cost, not just factor-base size
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only under the original record restriction; 4 CPU-hour cap. Do not issue a universal dimension-obstruction receipt for arbitrary finite algebraic conditions.

records.hypothesis: The named cover/index-calculus implementation fails to beat direct rho on its measured E-component instances.
steps: Use the checked split genus-two covers as map/point-count controls, then implement explicit pullback/projection on Jacobians.
Run the named genus-two algorithm with complete relation and matrix costs.
Add genus-three and descent-direction cases only after the same code passes known-answer controls.
controls: Direct rho on E
Verified split Jacobian order identity
Finite kernels and E-component membership certified
measurements: Size-dependent costs of the named algorithm
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only under the original restriction; 8 CPU-hour initial cap. An observed or published algorithmic upper bound is not a lower bound for every algorithm.

records.hypothesis: Typical class-number and local-lift costs can be measured after certifying End(E); rational/small-CM exceptions are separate.
steps: Compute the actual endomorphism order on a small certified curve sample, not only the Frobenius order.
Record both h(D) and the correct global field degree; define all conductor indices.
For a selected family, compare canonical-lift algorithms and rational-approximation heights, including exact rational-CM controls.
controls: Known class-number tables
The exact rational CM exception already checked
Supersingular cases excluded and counted
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; 100 curves per small size, 8 CPU-hour cap. Current Frobenius-order samples do not certify global canonical-lift degrees.

records.hypothesis: After separating fixed small Teichmuller representatives, smoothness of truncated lifts can be compared with matched-size unit integers.
steps: Repeat at five small primes, several k, and B selected to produce measurable event counts.
Report the atom omega(1)=1 separately; predeclare whether other small representatives are excluded.
Compare both the uniform-unit finite distribution and any Dickman approximation, with finite-size errors explicit.
controls: Naive representatives at k=1
Uniform units modulo p^k
Exact multiplicativity and Frobenius-fixedness checks
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only under the original restriction; 2 CPU-hour cap. Do not interpret a one-event floor as an asymptotic smoothness advantage.

records.hypothesis: Certified lattice counts give a necessary coverage budget depending on rank, regulator, factor-base size and m; actual specialization can lose coverage.
steps: Import exact point/independence/saturation certificates before claiming full high-rank MW lattices.
Validate enumeration against exact or independently checked lattice counts at manageable ranks.
Tabulate r >= log(target_count/|F|)/log(m) with every parameter and L-function constant specified, then measure small-prime specialization.
controls: The exact cyclic-sublattice pilot
Random lattices with matched Gram determinant
Independent lattice enumeration
records.stopping_rule: 8 CPU-hour initial cap; restrict enumeration by an operation/point budget. Current evidence is rank one and cannot validate rank-31 or cryptographic coverage claims.

records.hypothesis: A specified lift ensemble has measurable rank/height statistics; generic surface rank and Lang-type statements do not bound every specialization.
steps: Predeclare a lift sampling distribution and matched conductor/minimal-model controls.
Use certified descent bounds and verified points; retain unresolved rank intervals.
Separate fixed small-coefficient lifts from the random ensemble and measure reduced-point coverage from an explicitly enumerated subset.
controls: The fixed curve y^2=x^3-2
Matched conductor range
Height normalization and conditional theorem hypotheses
measurements: Generator-height bounds, not just found-point heights
Coverage lower bounds versus certified exhaustive coverage
records.stopping_rule: 8 CPU-hour initial cap and 200 lifts per small prime. No full-rank or full-factor-base claim without certificates.

records.hypothesis: Nontrivial small relations in fitted lifts remain rare once duplicates and single-point torsion are stratified.
steps: Repeat k=2 with a predeclared sampling law, excluding or separately counting zero-y torsion cases.
Give explicit k=3,4 fitting families before comparing their dependence rates.
Recover candidate relations exactly and verify them in the rational group; certify rank intervals independently.
controls: Planted relation 2P-Q=O
Single-point torsion stratum
Unfitted matched rational curves
measurements: Trivial torsion relations versus two-point dependencies
records.stopping_rule: 4 CPU-hour pilot cap. Nine current small relations are single-point 2-torsion, not new xedni successes; absence of coefficients up to two does not prove independence.

records.hypothesis: A predeclared, non-tautological small-prime feature can rank candidates for target-kernel membership cheaply enough to improve yield per unit work.
steps: Retire the original B-smooth(W) independence trigger: for B
Define features without using the target label or its p-adic valuation; match vector norm, gcd and subgroup-primary strata.
Train on separate curves/boxes and test on held-out target primes. Size the sample for at least 200 positive labels per test cell.
Compare feature cost divided by measured enrichment plus final target-test cost against direct W mod p or group evaluation.
controls: Permuted labels within the same strata
Random lattices of the same index
Known local-divisibility exclusions and shared torsion accounted for
measurements: Feature cost and completed cost per accepted relation
False discovery control across q and parameter choices
records.stopping_rule: At most 4 CPU-hours before a powered held-out improvement exists. Nonzero MI from the original exclusion is not an alive signal; computing W/p after detecting p|W does not discover the kernel.

records.hypothesis: No new low-complexity recurrence gives a completed period/DLP shortcut beyond the known EDS identities in the tested family.
steps: Record zero-apparition order, raw value period and normalization separately.
Validate linear-complexity profiles on EDS, ordinary random sequences and matched LFSRs.
Search degree at most three/span at most eight with held-out samples, quotienting out known defining identities and their shifts.
controls: The discovered defining quadratic recurrence
LFSR positive control
Known-answer period and point order
records.stopping_rule: 4 CPU-hour cap; no huge L=10*order run at 40-bit order without a feasible sequence/memory plan. Current search only covers quadratic span four.

records.hypothesis: Prescribed ordinary fibres admit explicit arithmetic-rank-eight baselines; useful rank growth under fibre-preserving constructions requires separate certificates.
steps: Extend the split cubic-pencil controls to 20 curves per size, with all base points selected before targets.
Try selected good-fibre-preserving base changes or twists with f(t0) nonzero; certify newly independent sections and their field of definition.
Record chi, arithmetic rank, geometric rank, Gram determinant, j-map degree and actual target-fibre isomorphism.
controls: The eight checked rank-eight pencils
Constant-j strata separate from nonconstant j maps
Do not use a twist with a simple zero at a prescribed good fibre
measurements: Actual j-image size conditioned on the certified family
records.stopping_rule: 12 CPU-hour initial cap. No random-surface rank inferred from ten point counts without a sufficient reconstruction theorem and a valid Tate result.

records.hypothesis: Certified family-specific height lattices can give small sections; no universal shortest-height interval is inferred from the Shioda formula alone.
steps: Compute exact Gram matrices, torsion and local corrections on any new E1 family.
Define lambda_1 versus lambda_1 squared explicitly and exclude rank-zero cases.
Compare prime-size dependence only within genuinely matched certified families.
controls: The exact E8 Gram, determinant one and minimum squared norm two
Independent intersection-form computations
measurements: Exact shortest squared norm and Gram determinant
Heights versus chi within the specified family
records.stopping_rule: Receipt-only; 4 CPU-hour cap. The existing chi=1 E8 result is a selected family, not a general regression over all surfaces.

records.hypothesis: A blind rational-section solver can improve completed fresh-target costs beyond matched generic/oracle group search on fixed certified surfaces.
steps: Freeze target-independent rank-eight pencils whose basis specialization logs are known from construction.
Convert to a denominator-inclusive section parametrization or an equivalent plane-divisor encoding; prove its height/degree coverage and compute exact basis coordinates.
Benchmark at five small field sizes with 30 fresh and 30 planted targets each; match actual target coverage, not just a necessary lattice count.

Compare a dedicated geometry solver and one general polynomial solver against rho and height/box-matched MITM. Charge construction, preprocessing, rejected candidates, coordinate extraction and verification.
controls: The 92-section interpolation pilot and its limited coverage
Complete E8 height counts and measured specialization coverage
Fixed-basis oracle MITM distinguished from blind solving
Matched planted random systems
measurements: Cold single-target and amortized batch costs
Output size, memory, regularity degree and actual height
records.stopping_rule: 20 CPU-hour initial cap, 30-minute per-instance wall limit. Continue a solver line only if its matched-coverage advantage survives complete accounting and held-out curves. Toy exponents never become subexponential claims.

records.hypothesis: Exact lattice counts and actual specialization coverage determine useful instance sizes more reliably than volume counts alone.
steps: Use exact E8 theta counts to validate enumeration and height conventions.
For new E1 lattices, record exact determinants and count short vectors with a finite operation budget.
Measure all-target coverage on tiny groups, not just N(H)>=p; distinguish worst-case, random-target and planted-target heights.
Compute high-rank synthetic tables only with stated Gram models and an actual E3 height-to-degree encoding.
controls: Counts 241,2401,9121,26641 at squared heights 2,4,6,8
Matched random lattices and subgroup image size
measurements: Necessary height versus observed quantile heights
Degree and unknown count only when encoding exists
records.stopping_rule: 4 CPU-hour cap; no conversion from lambda_1 alone to determinant, no cryptographic-height claim from an unspecified synthetic lattice.

records.hypothesis: A specified number-field lift ensemble can be compared with Q lifts after degree-one reduction and point/rank certificates are established.
steps: Verify d divides n, irreducibility of x^d-c, actual field degree and good degree-one reduction.
Begin with quadratic twists where rank decomposition and non-torsion points can be independently certified.
Keep fixed-curve K-points separate from random-lift ensembles; extend to cubic/quintic fields only with validated descent and height software.
controls: The checked K=Q(sqrt(3)) non-torsion point and actual p=2^n-3 reductions
Fields matched by discriminant and degree
measurements: Observed-subset coverage versus exhaustive certified coverage
records.stopping_rule: 8 CPU-hour initial cap. Current fixed-point receipts do not estimate average rank gain or full factor-base coverage.
